| Claim ID | Verdict | Closest Prior Works (DOI/arXiv ID) | Recommended Narrowing |
|---|---|---|---|
| C1 | **Survives** | **MATTERIX** — DOI `10.1038/s43588-025-00924-4`: chemistry-lab digital twin with real-world workflow validation, but not DES validation against measured per-operation handling-time distributions and intervention rates (pqac-00000018, pqac-00000020). **Lopes et al.** — DOI `10.1080/00207543.2019.1683250`: pharmaceutical-QC laboratory DES using empirical processing times and reporting aggregate time-in-system with simulation-run SD, but no operation-level spreads or intervention rates (pqac-00000041, pqac-00000043). **Tom et al.** — DOI `10.1021/acs.chemrev.4c00055`: comprehensive SDL review; no matching measurement-and-DES study found. | Retain the conjunction explicitly: operation-level handling times **with spread**, human-intervention rates, and DES validation against those measurements across a materials/alloy loop. |
| C2 | **Survives** | **Andrews et al.** — DOI `10.1007/978-981-99-3330-3_27`: KUKA arm and Ender 3 V2; part removal and bed cleaning each succeeded in 10/10 trials, but no CI or camera clear-check/false-clear metric (pqac-00000000). **Wang et al.** — DOI `10.3390/app151810222`: industrial printer-farm sorting system with large virtual trial sets and reported grasping performance, but not a sub-$5,000 arm or measured camera false-clear rate (pqac-00000025, pqac-00000026). **Li et al.** — DOI `10.1109/MRA.2021.3103478`: *Detect-Remove-Replace* robotic continuous-printing system; full quantitative evidence was not obtainable in this search. | State novelty as the **combined benchmark**: arm purchase price below $5,000, many physical clearing trials, binomial CI, and a separately measured camera false-clear rate using deliberately uncleared plates. |
| C3 | **Needs Narrowing** | **Burger** — DOI `10.17638/03087073` **[thesis/repository; non-peer-reviewed]**: mobile manipulator moved vial racks into and out of a GC headspace-sampler station, reporting 464/464 successful transfers in each direction over 71 iterations (pqac-00000002). **Carruthers** (2025) **[thesis/non-peer-reviewed]**: vial/rack loading and unloading around laboratory workstations, but no hundreds-operation success statistic (pqac-00000003). **Ochiai et al.** — arXiv `2501.05789` / DOI `10.48550/arxiv.2501.05789` **[preprint version; later peer-reviewed]**: self-maintainability framework treats restocking as “care,” but reports no primary restocking experiment or success data (pqac-00000037, pqac-00000040). | Restrict to restocking **replaceable consumables into the deck or storage positions of a gantry liquid handler**—for example OT-2/CubXL tip racks, plates, or vial carriers—with item-level success measured over hundreds of operations. The broader phrase “or similar laboratory instrument” is undermined by Burger’s GC-station result. |
| C4 | **Survives** | **Wojtkowski** — DOI `10.32920/32288082` **[thesis/non-peer-reviewed]**: PiPER study repeats the ±0.1 mm specification but performs no independent ISO 9283 metrology (pqac-00000001). **Chajón et al.** — DOI `10.3390/robotics15050086`: selected ISO 9283 elements, 30 repetitions at five poses, and external photogrammetry—but on a UR3, not PiPER or SO-100/SO-101 (pqac-00000031, pqac-00000032). **Oghalai et al.** — DOI `10.1016/j.mfglet.2026.08.019`: low-cost Annin AR4 calibration validated with dial indicators; not one of the claimed arms (pqac-00000033). | Preserve the named embodiments and require independently measured pose **accuracy and repeatability**, multiple workspace poses and approach directions, uncertainty reporting, and external traceable ground truth. |
| C5 | **Needs Narrowing** | **RoboBuilder** — arXiv `2611.23855` **[preprint]**: LLM/coding agents designed mechanisms containing custom 3D-printed parts; 135 robots were physically built and tested. Initial simulated passes achieved 0/15 real successes (44 attempts), rising to 73% after simulator learning and 93% after hardware-loop redesign; these were locomotion mechanisms, not laboratory fixtures (pqac-00000045, pqac-00000046, pqac-00000047). **Ocker et al.** — arXiv `2503.04417` **[preprint]**: LLM-driven multi-agent CAD aimed partly at 3D printing, without real laboratory-robot validation. **Yoshikawa et al.** — DOI `10.1007/s10514-023-10136-2`: LLM-generated chemistry-robot plans executed physically, but no fixture design. | Limit novelty to an LLM agent designing a **laboratory-specific fixture, holder, or instrument-to-robot adapter**, printed and tested on a real laboratory robot, with predefined fit/function criteria and a matched human-designed baseline. Do not claim novelty for LLM-designed printed robot hardware generally. |
| C6 | **False** | **RaC** — arXiv `2509.07953` / DOI `10.48550/arxiv.2509.07953`: human takeovers during policy rollouts supply recovery and correction segments for learned long-horizon manipulation (pqac-00000012, pqac-00000013). **TRANSIC** — arXiv `2405.10315` / DOI `10.48550/arxiv.2405.10315`: records teleoperated interventions and trains a gated residual correction policy for real-arm sim-to-real transfer (pqac-00000010, pqac-00000014, pqac-00000015). **HACTS** — arXiv `2503.24070` **[preprint]**: collects online action-correction data through bilateral takeover teleoperation (pqac-00000017). **Mandlekar et al.** — arXiv `2012.06733` **[preprint]**: iterative human-in-the-loop imitation learning from remote takeover corrections (pqac-00000011). | The broad learning-from-takeovers concept is prior art. Recast the claim as the first demonstration specifically in a **scientific laboratory workflow**, where takeovers interrupt an otherwise scripted or fiducial-guided arm, train a recovery policy, and the intervention rate—with denominator and uncertainty—is tracked longitudinally across the campaign. None of the closest works found satisfies all of those laboratory-specific conditions. |


*Table: This table gives the verdict, strongest prior art, and defensible narrowing for claims C1–C6. It distinguishes genuinely unlocated conjunctions from broader concepts already demonstrated in laboratory automation, robot design, or learning from human interventions.*
